Subject: Private deployability assessment + exception request for Acme Health

Team — looping you all in on a firm ask from Acme Health (their procurement lead is on cc). They want a private, customer-hosted deployment in their VPC with on-prem connectors for a HIPAA-covered workload. They have requested:

- A feasibility confirmation (network, KMS/HSM, air-gapped option)
- A preliminary SOW and resource estimate for implementation + 12-month ops support
- Any exceptions we need to operational/retention defaults (they require 36-month logs retention)

Key constraints called out by Acme: must not send PHI to our hosted plane, HSM-backed key control, and a 99.95% production SLA. They want a high-level delivery window by end of next week.

Attachments: security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (procurement), network_diagram_v1.png (customer sketch)

Immediate asks for this thread:
1) Laura — can you confirm architecture blockers (network egress, airgap, ops handoff)?
2) Dev — rough build + run FTE estimate and timeline (weeks)
3) Neha — security/compliance gating items and whether we can accept 36-month retention or need exceptions
4) Rishi — commercial impacts (pricing uplift for dedicated capacity / SLA)

I want a short one-pager we can share with the customer and procurement that narrates the risks, the exceptions we need to request internally, and a proposed timeline.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 09:15 AM Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you all in on a firm ask from Acme Health...

Quick notes from an architecture perspective:
- "Private deployment in VPC" likely means our control plane will need to run with a tight RPC window to customer-managed networks; we need to confirm whether the customer allows outbound NAT to our control plane or expects fully air-gapped. If fully air-gapped, we need an on-prem control plane build (non-trivial).
- HSM/KMS: we can support customer-managed KMS via external key wrapping but HSM-backed signing of model artifacts is a gap today — will need an engineering spike.
- Data plane: To avoid PHI leaving customer boundaries we must ensure our prefetched model weights and KV cache do not cross to Redwood-hosted storage. That implies dedicated infra in their region with no cross-region replication by default.

Missing from the packet: a clear network diagram with BGP/peering or egress policies (the attached network_diagram_v1.png is too high-level). Can Acme provide a CIDR map + proxy/NAT constraints?

If customer expects us to own the on-call for production incidents, we need to price the support differently. If they prefer to run first-level ops with our runbook + optional on-call escalation, that's easier.

I'll outline the architecture options (control plane hosted vs on-prem control plane, data plane boundary models) and flag the risky/engineering-impact items.

-Laura
Laura Bennett

Thanks Markus / Laura. High-level resource & timeline estimate for a private VPC + optional on-prem control plane: 

Assumptions:
- Model: 4x A100-class GPUs per serving cluster (customer cited inference latency needs)
- Dedicated cluster per Acme environment (staging + prod)
- No cross-region replication; single-region deployment

Estimates (approx):
- Engineering build: 4–6 weeks (initial infra + networking + KMS integration) — 2 FTE infra + 1 infra SW engineer
- QA + compliance validation: 1–2 weeks (1 SRE + 0.5 QA)
- Run/ops ramp: initial 1 FTE SRE as single-point-of-contact, plus rotation option (3 FTEs for 24x7 on-call)
- Deployment automation and hardened runbook: 2 weeks (1 infra eng)

Risks / unknowns that expand scope:
- If on-prem control plane required => +3–4 weeks engineering and additional packaging work (connectors, bootstrap tooling).
- HSM-backed signing => vendor engagement (possible third-party integration) and +1–2 weeks to validate certificate flows.
- Log retention 36 months => storage and retention policies will add cost; need legal sign-off on retention of logs containing metadata.

Ballpark cost impact: add 20–35% uplift to our standard Dedicated pricing to cover the engineering packaging and long-tail retention/storage.

I can produce a short SOW draft with milestones if we agree on architecture direction.

- Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure

Folks — quick compliance checklist and gating items from security: 

1) PHI handling: We must ensure PHI never traverses Redwood-hosted storage or logs. That requires technical validation of our KV cache and any centralized telemetry collectors. We can ship a config that disables telemetry export, but that reduces visibility and will require an operational exception.

2) KMS / HSM: We support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS) with key-wrapping. For HSM-backed operations (FIPS 140-2 level), we need an architecture spike.

3) Audit logs & retention: 36-month retention of audit logs is acceptable, but we need to define what is in scope (access logs vs. payload-level logs). Keeping payload-level logs with PHI is not acceptable — we must ensure logs are metadata-only unless the customer signs explicit acceptance and we have contractual protections.

4) Pen tests & attestation: Acme requested penetration testing results and evidence for our SOC2 scope. We can provide SOC2 report redacted, but for on-prem deployments we'll need an MSA clause that preserves our IP and limits customer testing scope.

Attached: security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (filled with initial answers) — there are a few NOs or conditional YESs that require product changes or exceptions.

Recommendation: We send Acme a one-page risk summary that enumerates the exceptions we need to operate in their constraints (e.g., no telemetry export, customer-managed KMS, limited pen-test scope). If they accept the exceptions commercially, we can proceed with the SOW.

-Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager
